newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dresdner wants to manage Japan public pension fund.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner wants to manage Japan public pension fund.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said on Monday that it hopes to expand its asset managing business in Japan to start managing the untapped assets of Japan's public pension funds.
The German bank obtained 13 mandates of asset management business here in the past year, Gerhard Eberstadt, a member of the bank's board of managing directors, told reporters here.
Currently, the bank deals only with corporate pension funds in Japan, he said.
As of the end of 1996, the volume of the bank's asset management business in Japan totalled just over $1.0 billion.
Of that, the strategicly important corporate pension funds accounted for one-third, the amount of which had tripled during 1996, another Dresdner official said.
Japan's pension fund market is the second biggest after the United States.

The bank's asset management totalled to some $200 billion at the end of last year. Of that, Europe accounted to 72 percent, followed by the Americas at 20 percent and the Asia and Pacific region at eight percent.
Other business areas the bank puts emphasis on in Asia will be project finance and new issues, the visiting senior bank official said.
